Article Title: Medical device industry seeks rethink of draft law, urges separate regulatory body
Article Text:
The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. (Representative Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The domestic medical device industry, along with hospitals and healthcare providers, has urged govt to re-examine the Draft Drugs, Medical Devices & Cosmetics Bill, 2026."The Bill in its present form, does not provide the regulatory foundation required for India's medical devices sector to grow, innovate, and compete globally", an industry expert told TOI.The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and consolidate laws related to import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to ensure their quality, safety and efficacy.In a letter to govt, the associations say that the draft bill, in its current form, treats medical devices as an adjunct to pharmaceuticals, despite clear scientific, engineering, and regulatory distinction between the two.Medical devices are engineering products, and should not be clubbed with pharmaceuticals, the letter says, adding the draft Bill continues to use drug-centric terminology such as "adulterated", "spurious"."misbranded", and applies pharma-style criminalisation to engineering deviations.Globally, medical devices are regulated through risk-based conformity assessment and quality management systems.Further, the Bill does not provide for a dedicated regulatory authority for medical devices, despite repeated recommendations.In 2023, the Association of Indian Medical Device Industry argued that proposed overarching legislation (such as the Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics draft) fails the domestic sector by continuing to regulate medical devices as "drugs" under a joint framework, instead of establishing an independent, specialized regulatory body.Administrative enforcement including recalls, corrective actions, civil penalties-- should replace imprisonment for technical lapses, the letter by 11 associations including Aimed, AHPI (Association of Healthcare Providers India), ADMI (Association of Diagnostics Manufacturers) and Patient Safety and Access Initiative, says.The Bill 2026 applies uniform penalties across all device classes, from low-risk surgical instruments to high-risk implants, contrary to global norms.It does not clearly recognise key medical device standards covering areas such as biocompatibility, usability and software safety.While the draft has been circulated to various ministries and departments, key stakeholders, including industry associations, manufacturers and hospital bodies, have not been adequately involved in the process, the industry executive said, adding it appears inconsistent with the pre-legislative consultation process.
Article Summary: The draft aims to repeal the existing drugs and cosmetics act, 1940. The domestic medical device industry has urged govt to re-examine the draft drugs, medical devices & cosmetics bill, 2026. "the bill in its present form, does not provide the regulatory foundation required for india's medical devices sector to grow, innovate, and compete globally," an industry expert said.

Article Title: Book three-nightstay in Abu Dhabi, get UAE visa free
Article Text:
Eligible bookings must include a stay of at least three consecutive nights and a return flight from India.

NEW DELHI: Abu Dhabi is offering complimentary UAE entry visas to Indian passport-holders between Aug and Oct 31, subject to certain conditions.Abu Dhabi’s department of culture and tourism has come up with a programme that applies to hotel bookings for a three-night stay in the city. It will initially support up to 20,000 visas during the pilot period.Eligible bookings must include a stay of at least three consecutive nights and a return flight from India. The programme is available to those departing from India who book a holiday through participating travel partners.“India continues to be one of our most important international markets, and we remain committed to working closely with our travel partners to make Abu Dhabi even more accessible for Indian travellers,” said Abdulla Yo-usuf, director of international operations at the department of culture and tourism.
Article Summary: Eligible bookings must include a stay of at least three consecutive nights and a return flight from india. The programme is available to those departing from india who book a holiday through participating travel partners. It will initially support up to 20,000 visas during the pilot period.

Article Title: Shield people from unlawful digital content, SC tells govt
Article Text:
The SC bench said such cyber crimes severely impacted an individual’s right to freedom of speech, the right to dignity, privacy and the right to life.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Union ministries of home affairs and electronics and information technology to take urgent steps to create a URL-specific and judicially supervised emergency mechanism to protect citizens from grave unlawful digital content.While disposing of a PIL by advocate N K Goswami, a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant said the petitioner in public interest had highlighted the danger from digital threats of violence, doxxing, exposure of minor children’s private details, non-consensual intimate/deepfake content and identity-manipulating digital impersonation.The SC bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said such cyber crimes severely impacted an individual’s right to freedom of speech, the right to dignity, privacy and the right to life.It said the petitioner had highlighted protections against such threats using internet, digital mediums and Artificial Intelligence existing in other countries and suggested to the govt to consider problems highlighted in PIL for urgent remedial measures.Goswami said given the misuse of AI and proliferation of social media and its reach, it was urgently required to create “a constitutionally compliant emergency mechanism against grave unlawful digital harms, namely specific threats, doxxing, unauthorised exposure of children’s private details, non-consensual intimate or Al-generated morphed content, and deepfake/digitally manipulated impersonation causing immediate grave harm”.He said he neither sought a blanket ban on any speech nor suppression of political speech, criticism, satire, parody, journalism, academic comment, public-interest reporting, or legal commentary.
Article Summary: Supreme court asks union ministries of home affairs and electronics and information technology to take urgent steps to create a url-specific and judicially supervised emergency mechanism. Pil highlighted danger from digital threats of violence, doxxing, exposure of minor children’s private details, non-consensual intimate/deepfake content and identity-manipulating digital impersonation.

Article Title: Army opens its establishments to students through 43 internship projects this year
Article Text:
The programme offers a stipend of up to Rs 75,000 that will be disbursed upon the successful completion of the internship

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian Army has opened its establishments to student interns through the second edition of the Indian Army Internship Programme (IAIP) hosted on the AICTE national internship portal and has expanded this programme this year by adding 43 specialised projects.The programme offers a stipend of up to Rs 75,000 that will be disbursed upon the successful completion of the internship and fulfillment of all program requirements. The final stipend amount will be based on the intern’s overall attendance during the period.The internships cover AI, cybersecurity, robotics, drones and counter-drone systems, hospital information systems, wargaming and simulation, and strategic communication. Through this internship programme, Indian Army envisions creating a strong ecosystem where education, technology and national service converge to prepare the next generation of innovators. The internship offers an opportunity to gain hands-on experience and professional exposure with the Army.The Army started the pilot project in May 2025. The specialised tech-infusion trials, which began in 2025 focusing on wargaming, simulation and niche research, has now expanded into a structured multi-project initiative across army directorates offering up to 43 specialised tracks.The Army has already received over 77,000 applications since the programme opening, and the last date to apply is set as Aug 15. “A student can apply for multiple Indian Army internship opportunities, but a student can accept only one internship offer letter. Before accepting an offer letter, ensure it is the opportunity that best matches student’s skills, interests, and career aspirations,” the AICTE website said.
Article Summary: Indian army has opened its establishments to student interns. The programme offers a stipend of up to rs 75,000 that will be disbursed upon the successful completion of the internship. The internships cover ai, cybersecurity, robotics, drones and counter-drone systems, hospital information systems, wargaming and simulation, and strategic communication.

Article Title: 'Disappearing Faces': Sadhguru's new book captures people of remote Himalayas
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Isha Foundation founder Sadhguru on Monday launched a new photography book called "Disappearing Faces", featuring photographs of people he encountered during his journeys through the remote Himalayas of Nepal and Tibet.Published by Penguin India, the book was launched by Union minister Mansukh Mandaviya at the India International Centre in New Delhi.The launch was followed by a conversation between Sadhguru and commentator Anand Ranganathan, exploring the stories and experiences behind the photographs featured in the book.“These faces represent an era that will soon disappear: faces etched only by sensory perception of light and darkness, heat and cold, of springs and winters - above all, uncontaminated by information that is disconnected from our senses. Our senses lead to a certain sense of life where there is no Non-sense," Sadhguru said during the conversation."These are the visages that represent life that seems rudimentary but is rich with strong experiences of the land, the winds, the waters and the people. Over the last five decades, year after year, beyond the beauty and wondrous nature of the mountains, these faces have drawn me into the deep crevices of the Himalayas," he added.Carrying a camera along the way, Sadhguru began documenting faces shaped by a life lived close to nature and increasingly distant from the cities.The book offers an intimate visual record of the people Sadhguru encountered during his journeys.Sadhguru first journeyed to Manasarovar and Mount Kailash in 2006 and has since returned repeatedly, leading seekers on the Himalayan pilgrimage. After undertaking his first motorcycle journey to Kailash in 2025, Sadhguru is set to return once again this year on a motorcycle, continuing his unique engagement with the sacred landscape of the Himalayas.The Himalayas have remained a significant part of Sadhguru’s life over the years, alongside his efforts towards human wellbeing, raising human consciousness and his commitment to ecological regeneration.
Article Summary: Isha foundation founder sadhguru launches a new photography book called "disappearing faces" the book features photographs of people he encountered during his journeys through the remote himalayas. The book was launched by union minister mansukh mandaviya at the india international centre in new delhi.

Article Title: Ethanol-diesel blending may not be viable, tests flag sharp drop in flash point
Article Text:
(Representative Image) Tests showed that ethanol-blended diesel did not meet the required flash point specifications (Photo: PTI).

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Blending ethanol with diesel may not be viable after tests by state-owned oil retailers found that it sharply lowers the fuel’s flash point, even as the govt is exploring ethanol’s use as an alternative cooking fuel to cut dependence on imported LPG.In a written reply in Rajya Sabha, minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi said oil retailers had conducted scientific evaluations of ethanol-diesel blending through their research and development centres in collaboration with accredited laboratories and automobile manufacturers.The tests showed that ethanol-blended diesel did not meet the required flash point specifications. The flash point was lowered drastically due to the presence of ethanol, minister said.In a separate reply, Gopi said isobutanol was currently not being blended with diesel.Govt, however, is exploring use of ethanol as a clean cooking fuel, which could help reduce LPG import dependence as well as provide an avenue to utilise surplus ethanol production capacity in the country.LPG Equipment Research Centre (LERC), a joint undertaking of Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL, has undertaken development efforts for clean cooking solutions based on ethanol, Gopi said.The initiative assumes significance as India imports nearly 60% of its LPG requirements and is seeking to expand the use of ethanol beyond transport sector. Govt has so far focused its ethanol blending programme on petrol and has achieved the 20% blending target.
Article Summary: Tests by state-owned oil retailers found that it sharply lowers the fuel’s flash point. Govt is exploring use of ethanol as an alternative cooking fuel to cut dependence on imported lpg. India imports nearly 60% of its lpg requirements.

Article Title: HasanAbi calls for permanent Asmongold ban from Twitch and YouTube as streamer feud explodes
Article Text:
HasanAbi says Asmongold should be permanently banned

Why I'm Gone

HasanAbi questions Twitch and YouTube moderation policies

HasanAbi has reignited a fierce debate over streamer moderation after arguing that Asmongold should face permanent bans from both Twitch and YouTube . His comments came after Asmongold defended remarks that led to his recent Twitch suspension. Hasan questioned whether major platforms still enforce their rules consistently, while also pointing to what he sees as growing pressure from political groups and online campaigns.During a livestream on August 9, HasanAbi responded to Asmongold’s YouTube video, in which the streamer addressed his two-week Twitch suspension. The controversy followed comments in which Asmongold described immigrants using dehumanizing language and advocated shooting people, including children, in a discussion about immigration.Rather than apologizing, Asmongold said he stood by his comments. That response became the focus of Hasan’s criticism.Hasan argued that Asmongold appeared to be testing how far Twitch and YouTube would allow him to go before taking stronger action. He also compared the current moderation environment with what he believes would have happened several years ago."It's pretty wild that I feel like this is a test. Right? He's basically testing the boundaries of Twitch to be like, 'Listen, what are you going to do? I'm not apologetic.I don't care. I said what I said. Go ahead, keep me banned if you can. What's wild about it is I feel like this is also testing the boundaries of YouTube's terms of service, too. Because I feel like YouTube back in the day would quite literally ban someone for statements like this one. "The argument places Asmongold’s suspension within a much larger discussion about platform rules. Twitch and YouTube have enormous creator communities, and decisions involving controversial political speech can quickly become flashpoints.Hasan also took aim at the business pressures he believes influence moderation decisions. He suggested that platforms may be increasingly cautious about taking action against prominent creators whose audiences could respond aggressively."Oh, my god! It does say a lot about how things have gotten as far as like corporate culture in general that this will probably be a slap on the wrist by Twitch because they are ******* terrified of angering the right-wing masses that have spent a good deal of time doxxing people that work for the trust and safety team at Twitch. It's like really ****** up!"Hasan went even further, saying Asmongold would likely have faced a permanent ban under the standards he remembers from previous years. He brought up Destiny as another example of a creator who, in his view, received harsher punishment for less serious remarks."This would be an insta perma. Like, there is no shot! I would say, pre-Trump 2.0, this is a perma. Like, Destiny got banned for less, which is crazy to say. Like, he got perma'd for less, and he definitely deserved it! So, I don't even know where we're at now. You know? I feel like this would be a ban on ******* YouTube as well! Or at least a demonetization on YouTube as well!"The dispute now raises a familiar question for Twitch and YouTube: where should platforms draw the line between controversial political commentary and speech that violates their rules?Asmongold had not publicly responded to HasanAbi’s latest comments at the time of the report. For now, the clash between the two creators highlights how moderation decisions can become political battles of their own, particularly when major streamers are involved.
Article Summary: Hasanabi says asmongold should be permanently banned from both twitch and youtube. His comments came after as mongold defended remarks that led to his twitch suspension. Hasan questioned whether major platforms still enforce their rules consistently. He also pointed to what he sees as growing pressure from political groups and online campaigns.

Article Title: Buffalo Bills address viral “obstructed seat” photos that left fans furious over new $2.1B stadium
Article Text:
Buffalo Bills address viral “obstructed seat” photos that left fans furious over new $2.1B stadium(Getty)

Buffalo Bills explain their position as viral seat photos create early controversy around new Highmark Stadium

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Buffalo Bills expected fans to leave the new Highmark Stadium talking about the atmosphere. Instead, many left talking about blocked views.Photos from Saturday’s Blue and Red practice spread rapidly across social media. Fans showed railings, stair structures and overhangs cutting into their sightlines. Within hours, the excitement around the $2.2 billion stadium turned into a heated debate among Bills fans.More than 51,000 fans attended the first public event at the new stadium, and many praised the steep seating bowl and the energy inside the building. However, the viral photos quickly changed the conversation.Several personal seat license holders compared the actual view from their seats with the virtual renderings they saw before buying. Some felt the real experience did not match what they expected after spending thousands of dollars on seat licenses.The Bills responded by acknowledging the feedback and promising further review. A team spokesperson told Sportico that Saturday’s practice served as an important test for the new facility.“Saturday’s practice was a great opportunity to test the new stadium,” the spokesperson said. “We are currently addressing internal and external feedback regarding the facility’s operation following the first event.We’ll uutilisethe next six weeks to refine any details as we prepare for the home opener on Thursday, Sept. 17.”That statement became the clearest indication that the organisation plans to make adjustments before the regular-season debut against the Detroit Lions.The controversy grew because some of the images reached millions of people online. One Associated Press photo from a seat not used for Bills games drew millions of views on X, while a compilation of obstructed-view photos spread even further. Some fans claimed the railings affected the first several rows across many upper-deck sections.At the same time, other supporters pushed back and shared positive experiences from their visit. According to reports, the team has heard from fewer than 1% of personal seat license holders regarding sightline concerns.The new stadium represents a major project for Buffalo. The Bills, Erie County and New York State agreed to the stadium deal in 2022, with $850 million in public funding helping keep the franchise in Western New York. The previous stadium opened in 1973.Architectural firm Populous designed the venue with a steep seating bowl intended to bring the upper deck closer to the field. Open concourses were also designed to maintain views of the action from many areas of the building.The team chose a canopy structure instead of a full dome. The canopy aims to protect roughly two-thirds of the seats from weather while also helping trap crowd noise inside the stadium.The Bills exceeded expectations in seat-license sales, generating about $260 million from more than 53,000 PSLs. Virtual seat views played a significant role in that sales process, which is why the comparison between renderings and real-world views became such a sensitive issue.Ticketmaster identifies some locations as obstructed-view seats, but several buyers believe the warning did not fully reflect the actual experience.Most early reviews of the new Highmark Stadium remain positive. Still, the viral seat photos created an early public-relations challenge. Bills fans now want more than explanations. They want proof that the vast majority of seats deliver the clear view promised during the long wait for the team’s new home.
Article Summary: Buffalo bills address viral “obstructed seat” photos that left fans furious over new $2.1b stadium. Fans showed railings, stair structures and overhangs cutting into their sightlines. Bills responded by acknowledging the feedback and promising further review.

Article Title: Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick defends GTA 6's no-disc launch, says physical copies 'don't make sense'
Article Text:
Strauss Zelnick said the shift to digital does not mean physical editions will disappear completel

Physical editions of games will still exist: Take-Two Interactive CEO

Take-Two Interactive CEO: Disc version of GTA 6 may also come

Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick has defended Rockstar Games' decision to launch Grand Theft Auto 6 without a physical game disc, saying disc releases for major titles no longer “make sense for the consumer. ” GTA 6 is one of the highly anticipated games that will launch on November 19, 2026, in digital form, while physical retail boxes will include a download code instead of a game disc. Speaking during Take-Two's first-quarter FY2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick said the company's business is now "well over" 90% digitally distributed. "It's already a digital business," he said. "So, in certain instances, especially if it's a big game, discs don't really make sense for the consumer."He further added that most modern games already require players to connect to the internet."Also, in most instances, you have to register online to play anyhow. So, if you're already connected, who cares if you download digitally. It's all the same and it's much more convenient. That's where the world is going in our opinion, and I think Sony understands that. We certainly understand that."Zelnick said the shift to digital does not mean physical editions will disappear completely."It doesn't mean that we won't have physical editions now, and I'm sure that we will, in the same way that there's still vinyl in the recorded music business. But in other instances, it just won't make sense," he said. Zelnick’s comments came after a question about Sony's reported plan to stop producing physical game discs by 2028.In an interview with IGN after the earnings call, Zelnick said a disc version of Grand Theft Auto 6 could still be released later. "I wouldn't rule out anything at this stage of the game. What we've announced so far is what we're doing at the moment, but we are always open minded," he said.Zelnick also said Rockstar's decision was not driven by concerns about game leaks and that he does not expect the digital-first launch to hurt Take-Two's business.
Article Summary: Strauss zelnick said the shift to digital does not mean physical editions will disappear completely. Zelnick’s comments came after a question about sony's reported plan to stop producing physical game discs by 2028. Grand theft auto 6 is one of the highly anticipated games that will launch on november 19, 2026, in digital form.

Article Title: Why vintage collectors are reviving computers from the 1980s
Article Text:
Vintage computer festivals bring collectors together (Image source: AP)

Vintage computer festivals bring collectors together

Software engineer Josh Dersch loves old computers. He spends countless hours tinkering in his garage, trying to coax decades-old machines back to life. He estimates he owns more than 200 vintage computers and devices in his Seattle home.“It’s always been fascinating to me to see the origins of things,” Dersch said. “It’s a fun challenge to debug and repair. You can understand the entire system from top to bottom.”Dersch is part of a growing community of vintage computer collectors who are preserving the classic machines that helped launch the digital revolution. While Silicon Valley has since moved on to shaping the future of artificial intelligence, these hardware enthusiasts are intent on saving the Atari, Commodore and IBM machines that are ancestors to today’s laptops, wearable devices and smartphones.Where others see junk, people like Dersch see artifacts of computer history that are worthy of attention and respect. They delight in hearing the beeps and chimes of their childhood and firing up a low-def game of “Pong” or “Space Invaders.”“The enthusiasm for the history of computers and all the stuff around it is growing,” said Erik Klein, president of the Vintage Computer Federation, which organizes an annual festival at the Computer History Museum in Mountain View in the heart of Silicon Valley.This year more than 3,500 people attended the two-day Vintage Computer Festival in early August that celebrated the 50th anniversary of Apple, founded in 1976 in nearby Cupertino, Calif. It featured a panel with co-founders Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne reminiscing about the company’s early days as a scrappy startup led by the late Steve Jobs.More than a dozen such gatherings have since sprung up in cities across North America, South America and Europe.Growing interest is reflected in more demand for vintage computers in online marketplaces, Klein said. Rare, iconic computers like the Apple-1 — the company’s first product — can fetch hundreds of thousands of dollars.Collectors exhibited the computer systems that they have painstakingly restored to their original working condition, allowing attendees to play with the computers built long before the internet, social media and AI transformed the world.Restoring the ‘grandfather of the modern computer’Dersch drove down from Seattle to showcase the pride of his collection: the Xerox Alto. He spent years restoring what’s considered “the grandfather of the modern computer,” which was developed at the pioneering Xerox Palo Alto Research Center in the 1970s.The Alto was one of the earliest computers to move beyond text on screen and use the mouse and graphical user interface — such as windows, icons and cursors — that became the industry standard. The model famously inspired Jobs and Bill Gates to incorporate the technologies in their early products.Dersch’s exhibit featured a fully functioning Xerox Alto workstation with its boxy vertical monitor, chunky keyboard and mouse, as well as pizza-sized spinning disks that store tiny amounts of data by modern standards.“It’s fun to share what I’ve done with people. It’s fun to share in what other people have done,” Dersch said. “Also, there’s a consignment area where I can buy more junk to take home with me, so that’s always fun.”Klein, a Silicon Valley software engineering manager, was a passionate collector until his hobby overwhelmed his home and family life. He had as many as 150 computer systems — complete with accessories, documents and packaging — crammed into his closets and garage.He said his beloved collection had become an “albatross” and he worried about burdening his family. So he started selling and giving away his machines until he only had a few favorites left at home.Similar events for collectors spread around the worldNow Klein channels his passion for vintage computers into organizing festivals, repair workshops, swap meets and other events as president of the Vintage Computer Federation.“So it’s really about evangelizing that history and evangelizing this hobby of maintaining, collecting and enjoying this vintage technology,” Klein said.Sellam Ismail is thrilled to see the collector community develop and mature since he organized the first festival in 1997, drawing about 150 hobbyists to a venue east of San Francisco. He ran the events for a decade.He later co-founded the Vintage Computer Federation, which runs festivals in the US and Canada. He’s helped other groups launch similar festivals in Argentina, Germany and Switzerland.“The community grew up. More and more people started getting old computers, started collecting them,” said Ismail, who once had a massive collection he stored in a warehouse. “Next year is the 30th anniversary. And I expect this to continue and grow even bigger.”
Article Summary: More than 3,500 people attended the two-day vintage computer festival in early august. The festival celebrated the 50th anniversary of apple, founded in 1976 in cupertino, calif. rare, iconic computers like the apple-1 — the company's first product — can fetch hundreds of thousands of dollars.

Article Title: Harvard scientists build a silicon chip that writes DNA with electricity, paving the way for cleaner gene synthesis and DNA-based data storage
Article Text:
Representative image

How the silicon chip works

From neuroscience to biotechnology

Potential applications

Challenges ahead

Silicon chips have long been the backbone of computing, but a Harvard-led research team has given them an entirely different job: writing DNA. As reported by Science Daily, a study published in Nature Electronics, Harvard researchers have unveiled a silicon chip DNA writer capable of synthesising DNA using electricity and water-based enzymes. The innovation marks a major departure from traditional phosphoramidite chemistry, which relies on hazardous organic solvents. The chip can simultaneously produce 64 different DNA sequences, each up to 39 nucleotides long, offering a cleaner and more scalable approach to DNA manufacturing.The project involved Harvard, the Broad Institute, DNA Script, and POSTECH, with funding from IARPA, Horizon Europe, and Samsung Research. Intellectual property has been filed by Harvard’s Office of Technology Development.The chip assembles DNA strands one nucleotide at a time. A temporary blocking group halts growth until removed under acidic conditions. By applying tiny electrical currents, the chip generates protons that lower pH locally, enabling DNA synthesis to continue. Each site is confined by concentric ring electrodes, allowing parallel construction of multiple sequences.This precise control makes the process safer and more efficient than conventional methods.Synthetic DNA is essential for diagnostics, genome engineering, and cancer research. Current methods require centralized facilities and involve toxic solvents. The Harvard chip’s water-based enzymatic process could enable portable DNA-writing devices, making the technology more accessible to labs and clinics worldwide.Interestingly, the chip’s design originated in neuroscience research, where it was used to record electrical activity in neurons. Researchers later repurposed its precision current injection technology to control chemical conditions for DNA synthesis, bridging the gap between brain science and biotechnology.* Portable DNA-writing devices for labs and hospitals* DNA data storage, demonstrated by encoding a 169-byte text* Synthetic biology and diagnostics with reduced environmental impactScaling the technology will require new chemistry. Current limitations stem from intermediate molecules drifting between synthesis sites during deprotection. Researchers are working on more direct acid-driven chemistry to overcome this hurdle, aiming for longer and more complex DNA sequences.
Article Summary: Harvard researchers have unveiled a silicon chip dna writer capable of synthesising dna using electricity and water-based enzymes. The innovation marks a major departure from traditional phosphoramidite chemistry, which relies on hazardous organic solvents. The chip can simultaneously produce 64 different dna sequences, each up to 39 nucleotides long.

Article Title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes an 'August request' to employees; says: Our shareholders are counting on us to ...
Article Text:
Accenture CEO Julie Sweet ’s ‘August request’

Investor concerns are the reason behind this urgency

Accenture has made an unusual move in order to boost business before the close of its fiscal year. According to a report by Bloomberg, employees have been told that they can carry over unused vacation days into the next financial year, starting September 1. The one-time policy change departs from Accenture’s usual rules and is designed to keep more staff working through August, rather than taking time off to avoid losing accused leaves.According to Bloomberg, in an internal memo, Accenture CEO Julie Sweet has urged the staff to push harder in the final weeks of the fiscal year. “Our shareholders are counting on us to deliver a strong quarter in Q4 — everyone can contribute,” she wrote. Sweet encouraged employees to find new ways to serve clients and originate sales — whether small, large, or “mega” — to help the company finish strong.According to people familiar with the matter, the vacation rollover is itself part of this broader sales push, since it removes the incentive for staff to burn through accrued time off before the fiscal year ends, in favor of remaining available to work through the final quarter.The push follows a rough quarter for Accenture. The company reported a 2% drop in new bookings for the quarter ended May 31, and forecast revenue of between $17.75 billion and $18.4 billion for the three months through August, falling short of the $18.47 billion average analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg. Investors responded harshly: Accenture shares fell 18% in a single day to close at $127.98 on June 18, one of the steepest one-day declines in the company's history, contributing to an overall 20% slide tied to the earnings miss.The disappointing results have deepened investor concern that Accenture's consulting-heavy business could be disrupted by AI in the near term, even as Sweet has described AI as a "tailwind" for the company. A Bloomberg Intelligence research note last month said AI remains the central worry for the services and consulting sector, noting that while Accenture's leadership has positioned the company as a long-term beneficiary of the technology, concrete signs that AI is actually accelerating client demand remain limited.Accenture shares have since rebounded to $171.11 as of August 7, though they remain down more than 36% year-to-date. The company’s August sales drive and vacation flexibility reflect its urgency to reassure shareholders and stabilize performance heading into the new fiscal year.
Article Summary: Accenture has made an unusual move in order to boost business before the close of its fiscal year. According to a report by bloomberg, employees have been told that they can carry over unused vacation days into the next financial year. The one-time policy change departs from accenture’s usual rules.

Article Title: As 'Demis Hassabis wanted to LEAVE Google alongside Jeff Dean' speculations go viral; Hassabis shares his message to employees in a long LinkedIn post
Article Text:
Demis Hassabis, cofounder, Google DeepMind

What Google actually announced, and why the timing raised eyebrows

Demis Hassabis’ full LinkedIn post amid exit rumours

“I've been working towards AGI my whole life and I believe it is now close at hand. It's critical that as a society we get the next steps right to ensure this profound technology benefits all of humanity and ushers in an incredible new age of discovery and wonder.

As we enter this pivotal moment, I've decided to step into a new role as Chair of Google DeepMind and Chief Scientist of Alphabet.

This will allow me to focus on long-term AGI strategy and accelerating scientific breakthroughs, including leaning even further into my work at Isomorphic Labs where we are making extremely rapid and promising progress on our mission to cure disease.

We've achieved so many extraordinary things at Google DeepMind so far and I'm very excited for this next chapter under the leadership of koray kavukcuoglu. I look forward to continuing to work with him, Sundar and the executive team.”

Deepmind's London-to-Mountain View shift nobody at Google will confirm

The Gemini delays sitting underneath all of it

Six days after Google announced that Sir Demis Hassabis was stepping down as CEO of Google DeepMind, the story that has stuck is not the one Google wrote. It is the one circulating through investor group chats and London AI circles: that Hassabis wanted out entirely, at the same moment Jeff Dean walked, and was talked into a chairmanship instead. The claim originates with the Pathfounders newsletter, which reported on August 8 that industry sources believe Hassabis intended to exit alongside Dean, and that Google management feared the twin departure would gut the share price.Google has not addressed the report. What Hassabis has done, three days ago, is post a note on LinkedIn that reads like a man closing a chapter on his own terms. It restates the AGI framing from his internal memo almost word for word, points readers to the company blog, and says nothing about why the timing landed on a Wednesday evening in London, minutes before Dean's announcement broke.The official version is straightforward enough. Hassabis becomes Chair of Google DeepMind and Chief Scientist of Alphabet, keeping his role at Isomorphic Labs. Koray Kavukcuoglu, DeepMind's CTO for years and now based in Mountain View, takes over day-to-day operations as SVP, reporting directly to Sundar Pichai . Notably, Google did not appoint a new DeepMind CEO at all. Minutes after the memo landed, Dean, employee number 30 and a 27-year veteran, said he was leaving with Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le to start Discovery Loop, a public benefit corporation Google will fund as founding investor and cloud partner.Alphabet stock fell around 5 per cent.The Financial Times reported on August 6 that the reorganisation moves control of Google's AI effort from London back to Silicon Valley, and cements the returning influence of co-founder Sergey Brin , who now sits near Kavukcuoglu's desk. The FT also reported that senior executives had grown frustrated with what they saw as Hassabis's lighter focus on commercial demands, and that his decision to release AlphaFold freely became a point of internal friction. A person close to the company disputed that any tension existed. A Google spokesperson separately denied that power was moving west, noting Hassabis and much of the leadership remain in London at the new Platform 37 offices.Fortune's reporting on August 10, based on three current and one former DeepMind employee, fills in the harder texture. Gemini 3.5 Pro, unveiled at I/O in May with a promise to ship the following month, has missed three deadlines. Engineers blame a decision last summer to deprioritise coding while Anthropic and OpenAI ran ahead on agentic tools. Staff described 60-hour weeks, burnout, and a leadership vacuum in which Brin was visible on the floor and Hassabis was not. June alone took Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer to OpenAI and AlphaFold co-inventor John Jumper to Anthropic. A union bid launched in May over the Pentagon contract is still unresolved.Pathfounders ended its item with a prediction rather than a source: Hassabis will have left Google within a year.
Article Summary: Google announced demis hassabis was stepping down as ceo of google deepmind. Jeff dean walked out at the same time, and was talked into a chairmanship. Hassabis posted a note on linkedin that reads like a man closing a chapter on his own terms. Google did not appoint a new deepmind ceo at all.

Article Title: G-Shock GravityMaster GWR-B3000 launched in India, priced from Rs 65,995

Article Title: Meta’s 'spy glasses' face resistance in UK; banned by restaurants, pubs and theatres across the country
Article Text:
UK venues from Wetherspoons to Soho House are now telling customers to take off Meta's £359 smart glasses.

Restaurateurs say guest privacy ends where the hidden camera begins

The 'pervert glasses' nickname is doing more damage than any regulator

Meta's LED defence has not convinced anyone outside Meta

Meta paid Kylie Jenner to make camera glasses look like ordinary eyewear. Britain's hospitality trade has decided they are nothing of the sort. A report in The Guardian says a widening list of UK venues—high-end London dining rooms, private members' clubs, the country's largest pub chain and a major theatre group—are now telling customers to take off the £359 (roughly Rs 40,000) smart glasses, or at minimum stop filming with them.The bans land at an awkward moment for Meta. Sales tripled over the past year, with more than 7 million pairs sold worldwide, and the company has been steadily expanding the lineup with celebrity-fronted designs. But the same discretion that makes the glasses appealing to wear is exactly what venue owners have flagged as the problem. A phone pointed at a table is obvious. A pair of cat-eye frames is not.Jeremy King, who runs London venues including Simpsons in the Strand, Arlington and The Park, told The Guardian he would never knowingly permit "any invasion of guest privacy other than with the eyes we were born with." Soho House confirmed filming is not allowed inside its private members' clubs, and staff can be expected to ask wearers to remove the glasses. ATG Theatres, which operates the Bristol Hippodrome, the Edinburgh Playhouse and several London houses, said the same applies during performances.Wetherspoons, with roughly 800 pubs across England and Ireland, has taken a softer line that arrives at the same place. Chief executive Tim Martin said the standard rule in his pubs, and most pubs, is that customers cannot film staff or other patrons without permission—and that the glasses appear to breach that rule by enabling surreptitious surveillance.His instinct, he said, is to tell people to switch the cameras off. Notably, phones are not banned. The distinction is intent: a phone can record people covertly, while glasses are built to.The UK restrictions follow months of reputational bleeding. The glasses have been rebranded online as "pervert glasses," a term that stuck after reports of men filming women without consent for pickup-artist content. One woman told the BBC a man recorded her and then demanded payment to take the videos down. Instagram head Adam Mosseri has said the platform will remove harassment content shot on the devices.Musician Lorde attacked them from stage at Madrid's Mad Cool festival in July, telling the crowd not to buy them. Activist collective Everyone Hates Elon has plastered fake Meta ads across London bus stops, one using an optical illusion that flips Jenner's face into a skull—a nod to John Carpenter's They Live.Meta's response has stayed consistent: every pair carries a capture LED that blinks while recording, it cannot be switched off, and the camera disables itself if the light is covered or damaged. The company says people use the glasses for music, live translation and hands-free calls.Not every operator is hostile. Michelin-starred chef Tom Kerridge told The Guardian he has no issue with them, arguing filming is simply part of modern life and can be used creatively.The bans matter beyond Meta. Courtrooms in New York, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin have already prohibited the devices, and Bloomberg reports Apple is delaying its own glasses partly to rework its privacy pitch before a WWDC 2027 unveiling. The category's biggest obstacle is no longer battery life. It is being allowed indoors.
Article Summary: Uk venues from wetherspoons to soho house are now telling customers to take off meta's £359 smart glasses. Restaurateurs say guest privacy ends where the hidden camera begins. Sales tripled over the past year, with more than 7 million pairs sold worldwide.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.
